messages:
marta: Quick cross-team sync request — we need a spec for a per-customer "watchlist" dashboard and noisy-neighbor signals. Runtime/infra inputs + a simple UX. Can eng-runtime + infra + platform weigh in?
kenji: Happy to. High-level runtime inputs we can emit today: `tenant.qps`, `tenant.tokens_per_min`, `tenant.p50/p95/p99_latency_ms`, `kv_cache.hit_rate`, `batch.size_distribution` (histogram), `model.fallback.count`, `gpu.util_pct`, `gpu.mem_pct`, `rate_limit.denied_count`.
oliver: From infra side: we can add `node.gpu_steal` and per-pod `oom_kill` events and forward per-tenant routing decisions that hit the shard (we currently tag requests with `tenant_hash_mod`). But we need to decide whether to attach `tenant_id` in logs or a pseudonymized tenant key for privacy.
sarah: Product: UX asks — per-customer toggle, watchlist with pinned tenants, time-range quick-select, and a short explanation of why a tenant is flagged. Need to be careful with customer-facing vs internal views. Enterprise customers want a protected view (RBAC).
jamal: Platform: two API debates to resolve: 1) telemetry header vs payload field for tenant_id — header `X-Redwood-Tenant` is easy but some infra proxies strip custom headers. 2) Do we aggregate metrics at ingestion (metric labels include tenant_id) or separate tenant-lookup service? Aggregating is cheaper for dashboards but increases cardinality.
emily: Customer-success: we need per-customer SLO dashboards we can share with customers (read-only) and an internal watchlist that flags noisy neighbors that could be throttled. Also need a CSV export for account teams.
nina: SRE note: detection heuristics should be explicit. My proposal: noisy neighbor alert if any of these occur within a 5-min window: (A) sustained `tenant.p99_latency_ms` > 500ms AND `tenant.qps` > baseline*2, OR (B) `gpu.util_pct` delta > 40% vs cluster median with `gpu.mem_pct` > 80%, OR (C) `batch.size_distribution` variance spike > 3 sigma. Add a cooldown to avoid flapping.
kenji: Implementation details: emit metrics with `tenant_id` tag for short-term retention (14d) and rollup to `org_p30` aggregated metrics for long-term (90d). For privacy we can hash tenant_id to `tenant_hash` (one-way) and keep mapping in a separate access-controlled store for exports.
jamal: For dashboards: Platform will add a per-org filter, and a watchlist panel that surfaces top noisy signals and a single-click drill into logs + recent model fallbacks. We'll create a new API `GET /platform/tenants/watchlist?env=prod` that returns tenant_hash + signal_score.
oliver: Performance caveat: adding tenant label increases TSDB cardinality. We should only emit full-resolution per-tenant metrics for paying customers (or based on prod flag). Others get sampled metrics. Need signoff on sampling policy.
sarah: Product decision: sample non-enterprise tenants at 1/10th resolution by default. Enterprise (contracted) get full telemetry. Also need UI consent for customers to opt-out of internal watchlist sharing; CS will handle communication.
emily: Agreed. Also please include a column for 'flag_reason' and 'first_seen_ts' in exports.
nina: On alerting — create two tiers: `informational` (auto-watchlist, notify account team) and `actionable` (auto-suggest throttling or model fallback). All actions must surface an audit entry.
jamal: UX/rollouts: we'll ship watchlist behind a feature flag `watchlist_ui` and rollout via gradual percentage + canary orgs. Need `canary_onboard` list from CS. Also add a small banner: "This view is internal — do not share" for non-customer-shared dashboards.
kenji: Minor API thought: use header `X-Redwood-Tenant` for request routing, but for telemetry prefer `tenant_hash` as a metric label to avoid PII leakage. Keep mapping service optional and access-protected.
oliver: Ops: we'll add a retention policy and a housekeeping job to drop per-tenant high-card metrics older than 14d unless flagged. Also add cost tags so finance knows the telemetry ingestion delta.
marta: Next steps: jamal to draft the dashboard wireframe + API contract, kenji to list runtime metric names & cardinality estimate, oliver to propose sampling/retention policy, nina to write alert rules, sarah/emily to define customer UX & canary list. Can everyone ack by EOD?
jamal: Ack. I'll drop an initial OpenAPI fragment and Figma link later today.
kenji: Ack — will post metric list and example prometheus/metricsproto names.
oliver: Ack — will propose retention numbers and estimated storage delta.
sarah: Ack. Will send canary org list and UI copy.
emily: Ack.
nina: Ack.
infra-bot: Deployed: `telemetry-ingestor` config v2.3.1 to prod (sha: f9a3b2d). No downtime reported.
